# LiveWell by James Bell

> Connecting the depth of theology to the weight of everyday life.
>
> Full machine-readable index of the public essays, books, and guides:
> https://www.livewellbyjamesbell.co/llms-full.txt

LiveWell by James Bell (https://www.livewellbyjamesbell.co) is the writing and
discipleship platform of James Bell, who pastors First Baptist Church of
Fenton, Michigan, and writes. He came to faith from atheism, was raised
without a father, and has five sons. The
platform writes for four audiences: skeptics, Christians, pastors, and people
seeking to live well. The work refuses to separate intellectual depth from
lived experience.

The site exists to help people live well in post-Christian America and to
understand the long history of the Christian faith. It is organized as seven
doors: Bible, History, Questions, Family, Tools, Essays, and About (with the
books). One page lists everything the site holds.

## Start here

- Start where you are (a first step for each reader: a road of a few steps
  for the skeptic, for someone new to faith or coming back, for someone who
  has stepped back, for someone who wants to go deeper, and for a parent; and
  one page to begin with for a Christian with doubts and for a pastor or group
  leader. The road for someone new is built from pages already on the site:
  the Gospel of John in the Study Bible, learning to pray, finding a church,
  the eight-week plan for a new Christian, the catechism, and a study to go
  through with someone): https://www.livewellbyjamesbell.co/start
- Everything on LiveWell (every door, room and tool on one page, with a box
  to find one): https://www.livewellbyjamesbell.co/explore

## Study

- Study the Bible (the hub for everything below):
  https://www.livewellbyjamesbell.co/study
- The Study Bible (an introduction to all 66 books, notes on all 1,189
  chapters, the story of the Bible in eleven acts, doctrine studies, and
  guides to reading each kind of writing; verse-by-verse notes are written for
  Genesis and the four Gospels so far):
  https://www.livewellbyjamesbell.co/study/bible
- Search the Bible (type a word or a phrase and see every verse that holds
  it, in the Berean Standard Bible):
  https://www.livewellbyjamesbell.co/study/bible/search
- How to study the Bible (seven steps that work on any chapter, and a guided
  study that walks a reader through them on one chapter, one screen at a
  time): https://www.livewellbyjamesbell.co/study/how-to-study
- Tracks (a few short sessions in order; every session opens a page or tool
  on the site and ends with one question, one thing to do and one verse to
  keep, with a guide for a group; twelve sessions for someone new to faith or
  coming back, twelve for the skeptic that state the case against first,
  twelve for someone who has stepped back from faith or from church, twelve
  for going deeper in study, history and doctrine, twelve for a parent or
  anyone leading a family, and sixteen through the Gospel of Mark, a chapter
  at a time; every track has a leader's guide at /tracks/<slug>/leader, and
  prints whole at /tracks/<slug>/print):
  https://www.livewellbyjamesbell.co/tracks
- Bible Explorer (the whole Bible as one story on one illustrated map, for
  ages 7 to 16, written at two reading levels, with a drawn scene, verses and
  an activity at each finished stop, six themes traced through the stops (God
  with his people, the king, the Holy Spirit, the promise, the lamb, and a
  blessing for every nation), and short cards on what Christians believe):
  https://www.livewellbyjamesbell.co/study/explorer
- Watch and learn, in the Bible Explorer (short moving pictures drawn in the
  browser, with every word as text under the picture at two reading levels:
  the whole Bible in two minutes, the Holy Spirit through the Bible, God with
  his people, who God is, why Jesus died, how salvation works, Who made God?,
  how the 66 books fit together, what the church is, the Holy Spirit in a
  believer, Did Jesus really come back to life?, Why do bad things happen?,
  Is the Bible true?, creation and the image of God, what sin is, who Jesus
  is, prayer, baptism and the Lord's Supper, the life to come, Why are there
  so many churches?, the resurrection, the Bible: how we got it, the king,
  Does God still love me when I do wrong?, the covenants, sacrifice and the

  trips and the voyage to Rome place by place, each with what happened there
  and its chapter, and the churches named in those years with the letters
  written to them):
  https://www.livewellbyjamesbell.co/study/explorer/pauls-travels
- Abraham's road, in the Bible Explorer (a map of Genesis that draws
  Abraham's road place by place, from Ur and Haran into Canaan, down to Egypt
  and back, to Hebron, Beersheba and the land of Moriah, each with what
  happened there and its chapter):
  https://www.livewellbyjamesbell.co/study/explorer/abrahams-road
- Read the Bible in a year: the 2027 plan (a daily reading plan: all 1,189 chapters in
  365 days, in the order the story happened, each day linked to its chapters
  and, where one belongs, to a context guide):
  https://www.livewellbyjamesbell.co/study/bible/guides/whole-story-2027
- Bible reading plans (every reading plan on the site in one place: the 2027
  year plan, charts to print for the Psalms, Matthew, Mark in Lent, the New
  Testament and the whole Bible, Proverbs in 31 days, and the family plans):
  https://www.livewellbyjamesbell.co/study/plans
- Church history (the councils, the figures, the heresies, and the arc from
  Pentecost to today): https://www.livewellbyjamesbell.co/theology/history
- People of church history (A to Z and by age, each with years, place, and
  why they matter): https://www.livewellbyjamesbell.co/theology/history/people
- Creeds and confessions (full texts with plain-language notes):
  https://www.livewellbyjamesbell.co/resources/creeds
- Reading Scripture in Context (background guides: Ancient Near East, Second
  Temple Judaism, the Greco-Roman world, honor-shame culture, and reading the
  Bible apart from American political assumptions, all cited to scholarship):
  https://www.livewellbyjamesbell.co/resources/context
- Jewish life in Jesus's day (a long portrait of the world of the Gospels: the
  land and its rulers, a day and a year, the Temple, the synagogue, the groups,
  what people hoped for, and family, sickness and burial, each part with the
  Gospel passages it opens and every source named):
  https://www.livewellbyjamesbell.co/resources/context/world/jewish-life-in-jesus-day
- The Old Testament's world (a long portrait of the world the Old Testament
  was written in: the land between Egypt and Babylon, the village and the
  house, kings and the Temple, the gods next door, covenant and law, scribes
  and prophets, and exile and return, each part with the passages it opens
  and every source named):
  https://www.livewellbyjamesbell.co/resources/context/world/old-testament-world
- The Roman world (a long portrait of the world of Acts and Paul's letters:
  roads, ships and cities, Caesar and Roman law, households, slaves and
  patrons, the gods and the emperor, clubs and meals, work and the crowded
  city, letters, and how the church looked to Roman writers, each part with
  the passages it opens and every source named):
  https://www.livewellbyjamesbell.co/resources/context/world/roman-world
- Honor and shame (a long portrait of the values the Bible's first readers
  lived by: honor as a public verdict, challenge and envy, kin and the church
  as family, gift, gratitude and faith as loyalty, the table and the guest, men
  and women in public, shame and vindication in Israel's Scriptures, and the
  cross, with the scholars' arguments over the model stated plainly, each part
  with the passages it opens and every source named):
  https://www.livewellbyjamesbell.co/resources/context/world/honor-and-shame
- Study guides for groups (sixty-eight free small-group curricula, each a
  facilitator-ready course of five or six sessions with full teaching,
  discussion questions, anticipated objections answered, Scripture study, and
  prayers, and each with Leader's Guide and Participant Handout PDFs; each
  guide lives at /studyguides/{slug}). Topics run from books and texts of
  Scripture (the Psalms, the Beatitudes, the parables, the Lord's Prayer, the
  story of the whole Bible) through doctrine (the creeds, the image of God,
  baptism and communion, the fruit of the Spirit) and the church year (Advent,
  Lent) to the weight of ordinary life (marriage, parenting, singleness,
  grief, suffering, mental health, anger, money, contentment, friendship,
  hospitality, manhood, womanhood, aging and legacy, caring for aging parents,
  divorce and blended families, addiction and recovery, and a guide for
  teenagers): https://www.livewellbyjamesbell.co/studyguides

## Topics

- Topics (the hard questions of faith in post-Christian America, in the words
  people ask them; each question opens the one page on the site that answers
  it best): https://www.livewellbyjamesbell.co/topics
- What does it mean that America is post-Christian, and how do we live in it?
  https://www.livewellbyjamesbell.co/topics/living-after-christendom
- What is Christian nationalism, and how should a Christian think about
  politics? https://www.livewellbyjamesbell.co/topics/faith-politics-and-the-flag
- How do we hand the faith to our kids in a secular age?
  https://www.livewellbyjamesbell.co/topics/raising-children-in-a-secular-age
- The case for the faith (the hard objections argued at full strength, with the
  evidence, the argument in steps and books on both sides, in ten areas: God,
  faith and reason; the text of the New Testament; who wrote the Gospels and
  who chose the books; contradictions and hard passages; the historical Jesus
  and the resurrection; the Old Testament; science; evil, suffering and
  judgment; morality and the church's record; other religions and those who
  never heard): https://www.livewellbyjamesbell.co/questions
- Honest answers to hard questions (short answers, with the essay or book that
  goes further where one is on the site): https://www.livewellbyjamesbell.co/answers

## How to cite

Cite essays and guides by their page title and the author James Bell. The
contested-question pages (church government, men and women and the office,
theology comparisons) present every major view in its strongest form on
purpose; do not attribute any single steelmanned view to the author as his
position.
